techCategories.name: Tiered
techCategories.description: General configuration techs that have tiered proficiencies.

note: Ability to kill or dodge enemies with a similar level of precision as required in some of the later dungeons in the vanilla game.
This expects the ability to use weapons such as the bow or rods to deal damage, or even the Hammer or Bombs on slower enemies.
This also expects the ability to use the Hookshot or Boomerang to stun enemies.
Ability to kill or dodge enemies with precision while minimizing resouce usage.
This expects the ability to use alternate weapons such as the canes to kill enemies.
Expects refined and practiced movement to dodge enemies.
Expects high-precision dodging and full-room enemy manipulations to avoid damage.
Expects high-precision dodging and full-room enemy manipulations to avoid damage.
Expects high-precision dodging and full-room enemy manipulations to avoid damage.
Ability to fight bosses with a similar level of difficulty as some of the later bosses in the vanilla game.
This expects the ability to use weapons such as the bow or rods on a variety of bosses.
Ability to fight bosses while efficiently dodging and dealing attacks with accuracy to avoid wasting resources.
This expects the ability to use alternate weapons such as the canes, Hammer, and Bombs on a variety of bosses.
Expects a refined and practiced boss fight with few or no hits taken or wasted ammo or magic.
Expects high-precision kills that only come with practicing bosses with unusual weapons.
Expects high-precision kills that only come with practicing bosses with unusual, weak weapons.
Fights that should be theoretically possible but haven't been tested or precisely placed in the proper difficulty tier.
Ability to traverse simple dark rooms without the Lamp.
Expects simple room traversal with plenty of enemy damage leniency.
This is typically only included for strats with a good movement indicator, like a sword, boomerang, etc.
Ability to traverse dark rooms without the Lamp.
Expects precise traversal of simple rooms or traversal of moderately difficult rooms with enemy damage leniency.
This also includes the ability to know where torches in a room are which can be lit with the Fire Rod.
Depending on the complexity of the room, this may expect traversal with creative movement indicators, like the Red Cane.
Expects the traversal of complex routes through dark rooms without the Lamp while minimizing enemy damage.
This also expects blindly killing enemies which can move but drop a required key.
It is important to know the layout of the room and where enemies will spawn,
where pots and chests are and scripted movements for how to get into position to pick them up,
and how to recover when an enemy unpredictably changes Link's positioning.
Expects fully scripted and practiced movement through many consecutive complex dark rooms in a row without the Lamp.

techs.name: canBonkBoost
note: Dashing into an object, like a pot or wall, to boost backwards over a pit.
It is typically best to begin dashing while not facing the object, then rotate towards the object before the dash activates.

techs.name: canBombBoost
note: Using a bomb to boost Link over a small pit.
Requires positioning Link near the edge of the platform as the bomb explodes and pushes Link across the gap.

extensionTechs.name: canPreciseBombBoost
note: Using a bomb to boost Link over a 2-tile-wide pit, which may include a diagonal boost requirement.
This requires precise positioning of the bomb and getting hit while Link is at the very edge of the platform.

techs.name: canPushBlockClip
note: Using an item while pushing a block in order to have the item phase through the block.
This is typically used with Hookshot to pull Link through the block that is being pushed.
It can also be used with the Magic Mirror to delete the block entirely, in places where the mirror won't teleport Link.
Other items, such as the Fire Rod, can also be used but have minimal logical importance.

techs.name: canBreakDashableWall
note: A subset of bombable walls can also be broken by dashing into them with the Pegasus Boots.
The walls are visually distinct, with a circular crack pattern.

techs.name: canRiskPermanentLossOfAccess
note: Accepting that a change to game state may make a previously available strat impossible.
If the strat needed to be executed before that state change, the game may become incompletable.
The mistake may not become apparent until much later.

techs.name: canCrossRoomOverheadPickups
note: Using room transitions to obtain additional objects to carry overhead and throw, such as bushes, rocks, or signposts.
In the overworld, carry an object out of a screen and back in. The original object respawns while Link still holds the carried object, providing one extra throw.
An object can also be carried in from an adjacent room or screen to use where no suitable object is normally available.
In the underworld, it is possible to kill enemies with pots before resetting the room to to respawn the pots but not the enemies.

techs.name: canCarryLonk
note: Lonk is a fairly fragile character state which has more abilities than a normal bunny.
It is generally only considered useful in the Dark World with no Moon Pearl.
Lonk can use most Y-items and can move during many item animations. Lonk cannot swing the sword, dash, lift or throw objects, pull levers, or open chests.
detailNote: Lonk becomes Link after ordinary knockback recovery, including a Thief's shove, or after landing from a ledge hop or a drop to a lower floor.
Entering deep water to swim, receiving an overhead item or shop purchase, using the Hookshot or a medallion, and traveling with the Flute also turn Lonk into Link.
Ordinary underworld exits in the Dark World will lose Lonk and recheck Link's form.
A bottled Fairy revival converts to Bunny if the saved Bunny flag is set; otherwise, it converts to Link.
A damaging pit preserves Lonk if the saved Bunny flag is set; otherwise, it converts to Link.
devNote: The tech description assumes that Link has no Moon Pearl and is in the Dark World.
With Moon Pearl or in the Light World, it is assumed that Link's form is available, which it is considered strictly superior in this scenario.
Note, however, that Lonk is not considered inferior to Link otherwise, due to the Bunny Pocket ability.
FIXME: Fairy revival while swimming converts you to Link.

techs.name: canSuperbunny
note: Become a Superbunny by buying an item from a shop or by falling through a hole that leads you to the underworld or from the underworld to a lower floor.
Superbunny is a fairly fragile character state which has more abilities than a normal bunny.
It is generally only considered useful in the Dark World with no Moon Pearl.
Superbunny can swing the sword, dash, lift and throw objects, pull levers, and open chests. Superbunny cannot keep objects held overhead, swim normally, or use Y-items that ordinary bunny cannot use.
detailNote: Superbunny becomes normal bunny after ordinary knockback recovery, including a Thief's shove, or after landing from a ledge hop.
A Pegasus Boots bonk also ends Superbunny, but dashing without bonking preserves it.
Ordinary underworld exits in the Dark World will lose Superbunny and recheck Link's form.
A bottled Fairy revival converts to Bunny if the saved Bunny flag is set; otherwise, it converts to Link.
A damaging pit converts to Bunny if the saved Bunny flag is set; otherwise, it preserves Superbunny.
devNote: The tech description assumes that Link has no Moon Pearl and is in the Dark World.
With Moon Pearl or in the Light World, it is assumed that Link's form is available, which is considered strictly superior.
FIXME: Fairy revival while swimming converts you to Link.

techs.name: canPearllessLink
note: Become Link in the Dark World without the Moon Pearl by converting a bunny or Superbunny form,
The simplest way is to have a Wallmaster grab normal bunny.
Additionally, from Superbunny form, use a rupee pull point, throw an item into a Great Fairy pool, or get hit by a Bunny Beam.
